rca of the issue: Frontend was looking sound — bug found was in backend integration. record_transaction in server.py:3835 inserts into db.finance_ledger (collection used by all read endpoints like /api/finance/ledger). However, upgrades.delhivery_sync_once.py checks db.transactions.find_one({reference_id, category:'order_revenue'}) to skip already-recorded sales (line 1422) and does the same for db.commissions. Because these collections are empty in this app, the guard always falls through and the function calls record_transaction again every sync. Reproduction: configure DELHIVERY_API_KEY, ship an order, run sync-now twice → expect two duplicate order_revenue ledger rows for the same order. Mitigation: change db.transactions → db.finance_ledger (with the existing filter) and db.commissions queries to finance_ledger filtered by category='commission' OR add a unique compound index on (reference_id, category) in finance_ledger as a defense-in-depth.
